Documentation → Plugin Studio: build your own → Your first script

Your first script, step by step

A complete tutorial — write a Python script app with a form that checks a list of hosts against a rule, returns a structured result, then calls an external API through a connection without ever seeing its secret; test it, publish it and run it from an app.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.script_library
📍 WherePlugin Studio → New app → Script
On this page
  • What you will build
  • Step 1 — create it
  • Step 2 — the form
  • Step 3 — the code
  • Step 4 — test it
  • Step 5 — call an API without holding its secret
  • Step 6 — settings that matter
  • Step 7 — publish and use it
  • Next

What you will build#

A script app Host check: the operator pastes host names and a required domain; the script checks each one, logs what it does and returns a table of results. Then you make it ask an external inventory API — through a connection, so the API's token stays in SATOM. About 20 minutes.

📌Required

You need studio.script_library. Scripts run in a bubblewrap jail without the database and, by default, without network — see What Studio code cannot do.

Step 1 — create it#

  1. Plugin Studio → New app → Script, id host-check, name Host check. The script editor opens with main.py.

Step 2 — the form#

On Form (Fields the operator fills in), Add field:

Name Label Type Required
hosts Hosts, one per line textarea yes
domain Required domain text yes

Step 3 — the code#

Replace main.py with:

from satom_script import inputs, result, log

hosts = [h.strip() for h in inputs["hosts"].splitlines() if h.strip()]
domain = inputs["domain"].strip().lower()

rows = []
for h in hosts:
    ok = h.lower().endswith("." + domain)
    log("%s: %s" % (h, "ok" if ok else "outside " + domain))
    rows.append({"host": h, "in_domain": ok})

result({
    "checked": len(rows),
    "outside": [r["host"] for r in rows if not r["in_domain"]],
    "rows": rows,
})

The SDK, satom_script:

Name What it is
inputs The form values by field name, typed (numbers are numbers, checkboxes booleans)
result(doc) One JSON document shown as the run's output (calling it again replaces it)
log(text) A timestamped line in the run's output (print() works too)
connection("id") A connection the script declares; SATOM makes the call with its credential
secret("NAME") A credential the script declares, from the vault, for this run only
tcp(host, port) A TCP socket through the sandbox proxy, only with network access

Click Check syntax, then Save. Other .py files you add are importable modules; text files are data the script opens by relative path.

Step 4 — test it#

On Test, fill Test inputs (two hosts, one outside the domain) and click Save and run the draft. You see the log lines, the result() document and the exit code. Every save is a version (Versions & runs).

Step 5 — call an API without holding its secret#

  1. Create the connection: Plugin Studio → Connections → New connection, kind HTTP, base URL https://inventory.example.com/api, authentication Bearer, and type the token. It is stored in SATOM's vault.
  2. In the script's Settings → Connections, tick that connection.
  3. Use it:
from satom_script import inputs, result, log, connection

inv = connection("inventory")
rows = []
for h in [x.strip() for x in inputs["hosts"].splitlines() if x.strip()]:
    r = inv.get("/hosts", params={"name": h})
    found = r.status_code == 200 and bool(r.json())
    log("%s: %s" % (h, "known" if found else "unknown"))
    rows.append({"host": h, "known": found})
result({"rows": rows})

SATOM makes the request with the token; the script never sees it, and only the connection's base URL is reachable, whatever the script's network setting. A connection pinned to an API Catalog version calls endpoints by id instead: inv.op("getHost", {"id": 7}).json(). A PostgreSQL connection answers .query("SELECT …", [params]), read-only unless write=True.

Step 6 — settings that matter#

Setting Default When to change
Network none egress only if the script must reach the internet itself (prefer a connection)
Timeout (s) 60 (5 to 900) Long checks; the runner stops the script after it
Credentials none secret("NAME") for a password the script must hold (prefer a connection)
Who can run it — The groups or people who see it in Plugins

A script that travels inside an app package must run with network None, declare no credentials and not use secret(), tcp() or write=True.

Step 7 — publish and use it#

  1. Publish: the latest version is frozen under its number; operators run that version while you keep editing.
  2. Operators find Host check in Plugins, fill the form and get the result.
  3. In a flow app, the Run a script step runs its published version with values from the form, and later steps read its result.

Next#

  • The full editor, versions, database fields (lookup, dataset) and limits: Script Library.
  • Write and test scripts away from production, in the same jail: SATOM Builder.
